title: LightOnOCR-3
idiom: 16th-century woodcut scriptorium, red ink rectangles framing each whole block of a pinned page, one crumpled page unmarked
hero_prompt: Sixteenth-century woodcut illustration, black ink on warm cream paper with a single accent of vermilion red, hand-cut wood texture, bold carved lines and cross-hatching, flat and graphic, not a photograph, not a 3D render, wide panoramic composition: a scribe in a plain cap stands at a tall slanted lectern, quill raised, copying a large printed sheet pinned to a board beside him; the pinned sheet is laid out in distinct blocks — a wide heading band at the top, two columns of text below it, and a small ruled grid at the bottom — and each whole block is enclosed by its own thin rectangle of red ink, four straight sides and four corners, like plots on a surveyor's map, five or six red rectangles in all, never underlines; his copy on the lectern repeats the same blocks in the same places, each also framed in red; on the floor at the far right a crumpled, torn, rain-stained page lies unread, entirely black and cream with no red on it at all. The print is rendered only as rows of tiny abstract marks.
icon_prompt: Linocut emblem, a flat single-colour black silhouette on a vermilion-red ground, no shading or gradients: a round reading lens held over a small rectangle of four ruled lines, with four bold corner brackets framing the rectangle. Bold, high-contrast, no fine linework, reads clearly at 24 pixels.
